newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast products flat amid quiet Fri. trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast products flat amid quiet Fri. trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product values were mostly flat Friday as players left the market early for the weekend, brokers said.
A weaker NYMEX this week put buyers on the sidelines, but sellers were able to hold their prices Friday amid a lack of activity and slight gains in late NYMEX trade.
"The sellers are trying to keep the market up," said one trader for a products storage facility.
Heating oil for March delivery traded up about a cent at 60.90 cents a gallon near the close of Friday's NYMEX session.
Front-month gasoline advanced about a 1.02 cents a gallon to 64.20 in late trade.
Few deals were done on West Coast spot market, with a cargo heard sold at 73 cents a gallon for March barrels of Los Angeles CARB-grade unleaded.
Bids for CARB-grade gasoline were talked around a penny off yesterday at 73 cents, while offers were heard about 75 cents, up a penny. Bay area material was about four cents lower.
Conventinal L.A. gasoline ranged about 70 to 70.50, flat with Thursday, with premium still carrying at seven-cent advantage.
Distillates in both cities were unchanged, with CARB diesel in L.A. notionally around 79 to 80 cents a gallon.
